Installation & timeline

Can I Live in My House During Floor Removal and Installation?

Yes, most homeowners stay home during flooring work. A crew clears 1,000 sq ft of LVP in 1-2 days by working room by room. Here's what to expect.

By the Sarasota Flooring Company editorial teamPublished 2026-09-18Updated 2026-09-18
Short answer

Yes, most Sarasota-area homeowners stay in the house during a floor replacement. A two-person crew clears about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days, so we work room by room, sealing off finished areas and containing dust, and most families are back to normal in a zone within a day or two.

How We Phase the Job So You Can Stay

We break the house into zones and work one at a time rather than tearing up every room at once. Since a two-person crew can clear about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days on a prepped slab, a typical living-room-and-hallway zone is often done in under a day, and you keep using the rest of the house while that happens.

Dust barriers go up around the active zone, and furniture gets moved room by room instead of piled up everywhere on day one.

A typical Sarasota home has enough distinct living zones, a primary suite, secondary bedrooms, and main living areas, that we can usually keep at least one bathroom and one bedroom fully available at any point during the project. We walk the house with you before the quote to map out that sequence.

What to Expect With Tile vs. LVP vs. Refinishing

Tile is the one that asks the most patience of you locally, since most tile can be grouted about 24 hours after setting, and needs another 24 hours before foot traffic and 72 hours before appliances or heavy furniture go back, per MAPEI's guidance. LVP is close to walkable right after installation. A hardwood sand-and-refinish is the most disruptive; oil-based finishes need up to 30 days before rugs and furniture pads return, though the floor itself is usable well before that.

If your project includes refinishing alongside new flooring elsewhere in the house, we schedule the refinishing work for whichever zone you can most easily avoid for a few days, since it's the step that benefits most from an empty room. Rigid-core LVP splits the difference nicely for anyone who wants to minimize disruption across a multi-room project, since it doesn't carry tile's cure-time wait or refinishing's fume and dust profile. It's one more reason LVP tends to be the default recommendation for households determined to stay put during the work.

What We Ask of You During the Work

Move small breakables and anything sentimental out of the active zone before we start, and keep pets away from the work area, especially on tile demo days when dust and sharp debris are unavoidable. If anyone in the house is especially sensitive to dust or fumes, we'll talk through which days matter most for them to be elsewhere, particularly demo day and the first refinishing coat.

We also recommend having a plan for pets specifically, a crate, a sitter, or a closed-off room farthest from the work zone, since even a calm dog or cat can get anxious around unfamiliar noise and strangers moving through the house for several days in a row.

When It Makes Sense to Stay Elsewhere

A whole-house refinish with oil-based polyurethane, a multi-material job spanning several rooms at once, or a household with someone especially sensitive to dust are the situations where we'd suggest planning a night or two away rather than pushing through it. For a single room or a straightforward LVP replacement, staying home is rarely a problem.

If part of your project involves floor repair from an earlier leak or damage rather than a full replacement, staying home usually isn't a real question either way, since that work is typically contained to one room for a shorter stretch. Ask about your specific situation at a free in-home estimate and we'll map out which rooms need to stay usable throughout the project. We'd rather under-promise on the schedule and walk you through each phase in advance than leave you guessing which day a given room comes back into use.

Related questions

Do you contain the dust during removal?

Yes, we seal off the active work zone with barriers before demo starts, which keeps dust from spreading through the rest of the house while you're still living in it.

How many rooms can be worked on at once?

We typically work one zone at a time so the rest of the house stays usable. Working every room simultaneously is possible for vacant homes, but it isn't the approach we recommend for an occupied one.

Is it safe for kids and pets to be home during tile demo?

We recommend keeping them out of the active work area on demo day specifically, since that's when dust and debris are heaviest. Once demo is done and the space is cleaned, normal use resumes faster than most people expect.
